proposed_records.rationale: The religious schism, a facet of the source subject, reinforced Louis XVI’s personal doubts and turn toward escape; popular religious opposition and royal alienation shared this cause.
proposed_records.source_facet: Religious schism and the clerical oath

proposed_records.rationale: Pius VI’s letters and their publication were received as condemnation although they stopped short of explicitly declaring it; this completed the religious rupture and contributed to religious counter-revolution.
Varennes enlarges émigré concentrations.
The émigré army expected to supplement foreign forces and relied on subsidies; withdrawal of support exposed its weakness, while foreign priorities never guaranteed Bourbon restoration.
Lay religious solidarity and persecution of refractory clergy contributed to Vendéan Catholic royalism alongside conscription and local material grievances.
Religious refusal and lay support supplied a setting for Breton organization and Church-and-king allegiance, alongside local grievances; chouan bands retained dispersed leadership.
The source treats the Royal Session as the first attempt to reverse the new claim of national sovereignty, while preserving its significant reform concessions.
Artois’s exile court at Turin became an organizing centre for counter-revolutionary plans, without making the heterogeneous émigrés a unified or effective force.
After Varennes, arriving serving officers transformed tentative exile drilling into substantial military organization at Koblenz.
The declaration’s association with the princes encouraged expectations of restoration, but conditional diplomacy and later failed support did not guarantee intervention.
The Nîmes Catholics’ defeat and martyrs reinforced southern Catholic royalist sentiment before the first large Jalès gathering.
proposed_records.source_facet: Nîmes bagarre and its regional aftermath

proposed_records.rationale: The source presents Favras’s extraction plot as early counter-revolution but distinguishes Mirabeau’s constitutional aims, despite superficially similar schemes to remove the king from Paris.
Assignat over-issue and depreciation damaged creditors, fixed incomes, business confidence and ordinary exchange, contributing to the Revolution’s economic disruption alongside other causes.

The limited and then general rights conceded to free people of colour in 1791–1792 concerned already free people; wartime emancipation of enslaved people in 1793–1794 was a different subsequent transformation.
The collapse of paper purchasing power and fiscal effectiveness aggravated hunger and resentment under the Directory, alongside weather, blockade and military requisitions.

Preserving colonial slavery contradicted the universal-rights claim of 1789, whose principles were embodied in the completed 1791 settlement; the qualification concerns that rights legacy, not executive design.
proposed_records.target_facet: Principles of 1789 embodied in the completed constitutional settlement

proposed_records.rationale: The king’s religious and political alienation helps motivate escape; route planning, the Saint-Cloud confrontation and distrust are distinct contributing circumstances.
The flight activates the Jacobin network’s emergency vigilance and defense of the Revolution; subsequent club division is a different consequence.
The Assembly’s kidnapping fiction and preservation of the crown allow moderates to complete a monarchical settlement; this is not the Constitution causing the earlier Varennes response.
Varennes heightens expectations and fears of foreign rescue that shape reception of later diplomacy. Pillnitz did not cause the earlier flight.
The king’s confidence in Bouillé provides a military component of escape planning; army mutiny as a whole is not a cause of the king’s religious convictions.
Loss of officers makes the army’s weakness and foreign intervention more alarming; it does not cause the diplomatic Declaration itself.

Lafayette collaborates with constitutional moderates in the final settlement; this does not erase conflict with radical crowds or transform his entire political career into support for one constitution.
